Storage broker methods must use SQL nouns: Select, Insert, Update, or Delete.

What The Standard says

“Language” — Brokers speak the language of the technology they integrate with. Storage brokers therefore use SQL-aligned operations such as Select, Insert, Update and Delete. read it here.
“Business Language” — The Standard contrasts broker vocabulary with service vocabulary, translating storage operations into domain operations at the foundation boundary. This reinforces why SQL nouns remain confined to storage brokers. read it here.

Why it matters

Storage broker operations use SQL vocabulary because the broker represents persistence mechanics rather than business policy. Select, Insert, Update, and Delete make that boundary explicit and prevent storage methods from being mistaken for service operations.

Bad code example

// Violates STXB007: Storage broker methods must use SQL nouns: Select, Insert, Update, or Delete.
ValueTask<Student> GetStudent(Guid studentId) => db.GetAsync(studentId);

Good code example

// Follows STXB007
ValueTask<Student> SelectStudent(Guid studentId) => db.SelectAsync(studentId);
